title: tiny-bench-logbook-julia
content:
Tiny Bench Logbook - Julia Park

Purpose: quick, per-session capture of tiny inference runs (ad-hoc checks, smoke tests, parameter sweeps). Not canonical; copy important rows to the team sheet later.

Layout: compact CSV-style rows for fast paste. Columns: run_id, date, model, quant, hw, batch, seq, latency_ms_p50, latency_ms_p95, tokens_in, cost_per_1k_tokens_usd, notes

--- data ---
run_2026-02-10_a,2026-02-10,redwood-3b,8-bit,rtx-a5000,1,128,12,28,512,0.045,quick smoke - prompt: FAQ chunking; kv-cache warm
run_2026-02-10_b,2026-02-10,redwood-3b,8-bit,rtx-a5000,4,128,28,70,2048,0.042,batched 4, small regen quality ok, watch p95 spike
run_2026-02-11_c,2026-02-11,open-gpt-l7,4-bit,rtx-6000,1,256,16,45,1024,0.031,lower cost but truncation at 2500 tokens - test with long context
run_2026-02-12_d,2026-02-12,redwood-7b,16-bit,rtx-a5000,2,512,48,110,4096,0.118,good stability, fallback to 3b if high load
run_2026-02-15_e,2026-02-15,redwood-3b,8-bit,shared-cpu-fallback,1,128,95,240,512,0.012,CPU fallback - large latency hit but cheaper; ok for background jobs
run_2026-02-16_f,2026-02-16,redwood-3b,quantized-4,rtx-a5000,8,128,62,150,4096,0.028,high throughput; quality regression noted on rare tokens - add eval set

--- quick observations ---
- p95 moves non-linearly with batch size when seq >= 256; falling back to smaller batches helps maintain latency SLO.
- 4-bit quant gives ~30% cost improvement on throughput runs but introduces occasional hallucination tokens in edge cases.
- CPU fallback acceptable for async ingestion pipelines; never for user-facing chat.

--- next runs (planned) ---
- run_2026-02-20_g: sweep batch=1..8 for redwood-3b@4-bit with seq 512 (focus on p95 > 100ms).
- run_2026-02-21_h: long-context test for open-gpt-l7 with seq 4096, measure truncation and token throughput.
- run_2026-02-23_i: compare cached prefix hits vs cold-start on customer prompt set (5 samples).

--- quick calc snippets ---
- rough unit cost calc: cost_per_1k_tokens_usd * tokens_in/1000 -> per-run cost preview. Example run_2026-02-16_f: 0.028 * 4.096 = ~$0.115 per run.

--- todo / notes to self ---
- Extract rows flagged "add eval set" into eval suite (eval/mini-regen-cases).
- Slack #infra: ask about GPU packing flags that changed 2026-01-30 (affects batch scheduling). Link ticket: jira:ENG-4821.
- Keep this file light; weekly prune and move stable baselines to shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/baselines.csv

--- free-form scratch (quick) ---
- saw weird 1-2 token repetition in redwood-3b@4-bit when prompt contains numbered lists. Might be beam/temperature interplay.
- Note: seed=42 in these runs unless otherwise noted.
- If I hit a reproducible quality regression, capture full input+response in /tmp/bench-captures and tag with run_id.

--- provenance ---
- provenance: ad-hoc local runs, sometimes via matt-runner container on devbox-09. Not authoritative.

(End of tiny bench logbook)
